reader_question: How are the House’s seats divided by party today?
grade_line: Documented: the House Clerk’s count of its members
title: Republicans held 218 of the House’s 435 seats on November 11, 2026, and Democrats 214, with one independent and two seats vacant.
measure_line: Voting seats in the U.S. House of Representatives by the party of the member who holds each, as the Clerk of the House counted them on November 11, 2026
notes: In the 2024 election, Republicans won 220 seats and Democrats 215; deaths, resignations and special elections since then changed the count.
A majority of the full House is 218 seats. Members elected on November 3, 2026 take their seats on January 3, 2027.
source_line: Source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, party breakdown, as of November 11, 2026, United States House; U.S. House of Representatives, Office of the Historian and Office of the Clerk (History, Art & Archives), Party Divisions of the House of Representatives, 119th Congress (2025 to 2027), United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Two seats vacant; the count changes with each vacancy and special election. The party divisions are seats as first elected for each Congress; later vacancies and special elections are not counted.
alt: A half circle of 435 dots, one for each House seat: 214 Democrats from the left and 218 Republicans from the right, with one independent and two empty seats set apart between them in the middle. A tick marks the 218th seat from the right, a majority of the full House.

table.caption: House seats by party, as of November 11, 2026

columns.label: Party, as the Clerk lists it

chart_notes: Every seat takes one ink, so no color stands for a party, and each block carries its name and count. The independent’s seat and the two empty seats, drawn as open rings, sit apart under the majority tick, each named.

majority.label: 218, a majority of the full House
